executiveSummary: The public site presents clearly and loads with a workable mobile layout, but search metadata, cookie consent, and form privacy disclosures need attention before a broader marketing push. Accessibility basics are partly in place; several interactive controls lack visible focus and name clarity. Security headers and TLS look sound for a brochure site. This is a sample packet — replace with live evidence for a real engagement.

scores.note: Thin meta descriptions; missing sitemap discovery path
Acceptable LCP on mid-tier mobile; hero not prioritized
Policy exists but outdated contact and form coverage
Focus and link-name gaps on primary CTAs
EU traffic not confirmed — needs discovery
No clear “Do Not Sell / Share” path if ads run
Same WCAG barriers; no Section 508 claim needed yet

priorityFixes.title: Gate marketing cookies until consent
priorityFixes.detail: Defer analytics and ad tags until the visitor accepts non-essential cookies; keep a reject path as easy as accept.

priorityFixes.title: Refresh privacy policy + form notices
priorityFixes.detail: Name processors, retention, and how to exercise California privacy rights; link the notice next to every lead form.

priorityFixes.title: Fix CTA link names and keyboard focus
priorityFixes.detail: Replace bare “Learn more” with destination topics; ensure a 2px visible focus ring on interactive controls.

sections.title: SEO
sections.summary: Titles exist on the homepage but several service URLs share near-duplicate descriptions.

findings.title: Duplicate meta descriptions
findings.evidence: Three service templates reuse the same 140-character description.
findings.recommendation: Write unique descriptions that name the service and locality.

sections.title: Speed
sections.summary: Lab LCP is roughly in the “needs improvement” band on mobile; images are the main weight.

findings.title: Hero image not prioritized
findings.evidence: LCP candidate is lazy-loaded and not preloaded.
findings.recommendation: Use fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image; preload the format the picture element selects.

sections.title: Privacy policy
sections.summary: A privacy page is linked in the footer but still references an old phone number.

findings.title: Stale contact details
findings.evidence: Privacy page lists a disconnected phone for privacy requests.
findings.recommendation: Update contact channels and document form processors.

sections.title: Cookie consent
sections.summary: Third-party tags fire on first paint.

findings.title: Analytics before consent
findings.evidence: Network log shows analytics beacon before banner interaction.
findings.recommendation: Load non-essential scripts only after affirmative consent.

sections.title: Accessibility (WCAG)
sections.summary: Structure is mostly semantic; interaction polish is missing.

findings.title: Bare “Learn more” links
findings.evidence: Four identical anchors in the services grid.
findings.recommendation: Include the destination topic in each accessible name.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: TLS and HSTS are present; contact form posts over HTTPS.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy yet
findings.recommendation: Add a staged CSP after inventorying third parties.

sections.title: GDPR
sections.summary: Insufficient evidence of EU residents as a primary audience.

findings.title: Scope not confirmed
findings.evidence: No geo or market data provided for this sample.
findings.recommendation: Confirm EU traffic and processing roles before claiming GDPR readiness.

sections.title: CCPA
sections.summary: California rights language is thin if advertising pixels are in use.

findings.title: Missing consumer request path
findings.evidence: Privacy page lacks a clear Do Not Sell/Share or request method.
findings.recommendation: Add a request channel and document ad/analytics sharing.

sections.title: ADA / Section 508
sections.summary: Public-facing barriers track the WCAG findings; no government-specific claim required for this sample.

findings.title: Task-blocking focus gaps
findings.evidence: Primary CTA loses visible focus in Chrome keyboard nav.
findings.recommendation: Restore a visible focus indicator and retest the lead form path.

nextStep: Schedule a Cybercon free assessment follow-up to turn these fixes into a sequenced remediation plan on Web Design & Development.
